name: Atmosphere
basis: A thin atmosphere of 95 percent carbon dioxide, 2.8 percent nitrogen and 1.9 percent argon by volume, the same everywhere. The grades keep those proportions. Known from spectroscopy and landers.

name: Polar layered deposits
basis: The polar caps are stacks of nearly pure water ice, with dust under about 10 percent in SHARAD radar profiles, and the richest ice on the planet. Grade is relative.

name: Mid-latitude ice plains
basis: Buried ice sheets tens of metres thick lie under a metre or two of soil across Arcadia and Utopia Planitia, and erosion scarps expose them in section. Poorer than the caps but far from the poles. Grade is relative.

name: Basaltic lowland plains
basis: Basaltic soil of about 45 percent silica, 18 percent iron oxide, close to 1 percent phosphorus pentoxide and 0.3 to 0.6 percent potassium oxide (Mars Odyssey gamma-ray spectrometer and the rovers). Grades are relative.

name: Meridiani hematite plains
basis: Opportunity drove over a plain strewn with hematite spherules, an iron oxide concentrate that stands for the iron-rich spot on Mars. Grade is relative.
